_comment: target_ns is aspirational; threshold_ns fails the gate. Values are provisional laptop bounds — recalibrate on the controlled host before treating them as the contract.

_reserved_ids._comment: Owners add the benchmark, manifest row, portable ratio where applicable, script production, and controlled-host baseline in one change. Reserved names are stable review contracts, not measurements of APIs that do not exist yet.

benchmarks._comment: #90 direct-index witness. The last entry of 4,096 measured 1.432ns against the two-entry table's 1.631ns; the same-run ratio below rejects a request-path scan independently of host speed.

Overage debit plus commit publication: the marker is visible before the phase claim and remains visible through committed-occupancy publication. Measured at 41.8ns locally; the same-run lease ratio below is the portable cost contract.

Stable committed-cap refusal, including the zero-delta publication RMW that prevents a stale marker observation. Measured at 7.7ns locally; this keeps the denial-path synchronization cost measured rather than inferred from successful reservation.

#90 eight threads sharing one lease, with an alternating commit/cancel mix. Measured 4.64us against 38.8ns uncontended; the wide absolute backstop acknowledges scheduler variance while the same-run ratio carries the portable contract.
#90 batched two-thread harness control: 4,096 bare authoritative CAS races per Criterion iteration, measured at 52.7us total.
#90 true commit/cancel race over 4,096 pending Reservations, with aggregate winner agreement asserted. Measured at 168.1us total; compare with the identical thread/barrier topology above.
Retightened for the foldhash principal hasher (#9). Paired A/B in one session: SipHash 23.6/23.6/23.7ns, foldhash 13.9/13.8ns — a 41% cut, and the largest single saving on the request path.
Same hasher change (#9), smaller share of the total: SipHash 74.5/74.6/74.6ns, foldhash 69.5/69.5ns. Moka's TinyLFU bookkeeping dominates its lookup, which is the point of carrying both.

#9: SipHash 115.1/115.7ns, foldhash 99.6/99.5ns. The 15.9ns saving exceeds the 9.8ns measured on the isolated lookup; the remainder is not accounted for by the hash alone. After #91's final always-tracked concurrency state machine, five controlled-host means were 108.91, 111.11, 107.86, 106.83, and 106.03ns (median 107.86ns).

Deliberately unchanged by #9. The foldhash side measured 2774/2784ns against SipHash's 3375-4085ns, but that baseline's own spread is 20%, so there is no improvement here this manifest can defend. Contended scheduling, not hashing, is what this benchmark is about. #3 kept it on the default single-counter topology: it is the layout nearly every deployment runs, and the sharded variant is gated separately below. #90 gives sustained contention fixtures a one-unit quote so governor's one-nanosecond replenishment quantum cannot make a fast runner rate-limit its own benchmark; the weighted-token check remains present.

#3, opt-in eight-shard topology, uncontended: the price of sharding when nothing is contending. Measured 116.6/124.3ns against the same run's 103.2/110.2ns default, so roughly 10-15% for the locality read and shard indexing. Provisional laptop bounds taken under load average 17-26; recalibrate on the controlled host.

#3, opt-in eight-shard topology under the same eight-thread load as admission/full_check_contended_8. Measured 446.4/618.0ns against that benchmark's 2.74/2.80us in the same runs — the contention the layout exists to remove. The portable acceptance bounds are the same-run ratios below; this absolute ceiling is a configuration/execution backstop.

#90 pre-#99 different-account baseline. Seven background requests and the foreground request use eight accounts, but today's engine-global counters still share a line. The sustained fixture uses the same one-unit weighted quote as the existing contention pair so it cannot self-throttle. Measured 583ns; reported honestly so #99 can prove the residual moved.
#90 different-account baseline with eight local lease shards, measured 201ns. The portable ratio below is the extra-lock witness: a global lookup lock serializes otherwise independent accounts.

Added with the request-path counters (#37) as the cheapest refusal there is: one map lookup and a return, so hashing was the largest share of it. Retightened by #9 — SipHash 20.0/19.8/19.9ns, foldhash 14.7/14.7ns.

Added by #1. The lease-exhausted path had no benchmark at all: `admit_once` uses a giant lease and cancels, so the quota step's failure branch never ran under measurement — and elastic mode adds a branch exactly there. This is the strict regression guard: the added match must cost a strict account nothing, and a refusal here is dearer than `full_check_denied` because it has already paid for the quote and the rate token. After #91 made disabled concurrency track both occupancies, five controlled-host means were 60.11, 55.98, 57.42, 56.44, and 56.00ns (median 56.44ns). Its row-specific 7% allowance covers that measured 6.5% upper spread without weakening any absolute threshold.

Added by #1. What elastic mode actually costs on the path it exists for: a compare-exchange debit against the cap, a reservation, and the matching refund on cancel. Comparable to `full_check` because it is the same work with a different counter — the overage counter sits in the lease slot the lookup has already pulled into cache. After #91 made disabled concurrency track both occupancies, five controlled-host means were 117.92, 121.43, 119.64, 117.57, and 116.95ns (median 117.92ns).

#91 optional request-count governor token with the weighted bucket disabled. After the final always-tracked concurrency state machine landed, five controlled-host means were 105.97, 106.51, 107.19, 106.82, and 106.22ns (median 106.51ns) on mistral-apple-m1-pro. The earlier 101.1ns row predated the two occupancy transitions and is not a valid final baseline. The absolute backstop matches the full admission path because this is that path with one unit-weight token.

#91 one locality-indexed principal occupancy transition plus one central bounded account CAS under the existing sustained eight-thread harness, with both rate buckets disabled. First limit activation drains pre-existing locality permits before using the central counter. Measured 3.25us on mistral-apple-m1-pro; the bound matches the default contention fixture and rejects another serialization layer.

Added by #2, and measured in `tollgate-auth` where the mechanism lives. The credential step after a cache hit: one atomic load and one constant-time comparison. Gated because a regression here is otherwise invisible — if the cache stops being consulted every test still passes and only the clock changes, while the uncached path measures ~800ns, 50x this. The threshold catches that collapse, not tens of nanoseconds. Laptop numbers, provisional like every other absolute here.

ratios._comment: Direct indexing is independent of table size. Measured x0.88 for 4,096 classes versus two; x1.5 leaves compiler noise but no room for a linear scan.

What sharding is for: eight threads on one account cost the sharded layout a fraction of what they cost the default one on a controlled laptop (x0.16-x0.24). A shared GitLab runner measured x0.88 because its scheduler exposed far less default-counter contention; x1.25 is the cross-topology backstop, while the separate sharded/uncontended ratio below still bounds the absolute contention cost.

The sharded layout's own contention budget: eight threads against one. Measured 3.8-5.0 under load average 17-26, where the foreground measurement competes with far more than its seven background threads.
Different-account default contention measured x5.70 over uncontended. A shared lock makes independent accounts serialize and breaches this portable bound.

Different-account eight-shard contention measured x1.42-x1.60 over uncontended on the controlled laptop and x5.55 on the shared GitLab topology. The cross-host x8 bound still rejects the deliberate global-lock mutant at x16.01 without pretending thread scheduling is architecture-independent.
Eight-thread lease contention measured x119.5 over reserve_commit; the bound includes scheduler variance but still rejects another global serialization layer.
The observer-safe overage transition adds bounded atomic publication to the same reservation CAS. A same-run ratio constrains that cost independently of host speed.
A stable overage refusal measured x0.20 against ordinary reserve-and-commit; even with its publication-ordering RMW it must remain cheaper than that successful transition.
The Reservation race measured x3.19 over the same batched two-thread bare-CAS control.
